# Naming fan-out partitions from any substitution source

`fan_out.partition_request` is ordinary substitution grammar. The partition set
can come from an upstream node's attribute, an instance param, the claim's own
payload, a typed message body, or a host-environment variable — with nothing
fan-out-specific in the syntax.

## The shared shape

Every template below declares the same node, differing only in where the
`partition_request` reads from. Each reads `{{child.partition_key}}` into its own
attribute, so each work unit reports which partition it ran as.

```yaml
  - type: fan_parent
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    claim_producers:
      - name: claim-producer-filesystem
        selector: data
        intent: rw
        alias: data
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    fan_out:
      claim: data
      partition_request: <the source>
      error_policy:
        kind: best_effort
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          pk:
            type: string
            source: "{{child.partition_key}}"
```

## From an upstream node's attribute

```yaml
nodes:
  - type: producer
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          items: {type: array, source: "{{params.items}}"}

  - type: fan_parent
    subscribes:
      - node: producer
        type: attribute/items/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    fan_out:
      claim: data
      partition_request: '{"list":{{nodes.producer.attribute.items}}}'
```

With `items` set to three entries, the fan-out dispatches exactly those three
partitions and each work unit resolves its own key.

## From an instance param

```yaml
    fan_out:
      claim: data
      partition_request: '{"list":{{params.items}}}'
```

```bash
rimsky instance create "$TPL" --params '{"items":[{"key":"p-1"},{"key":"p-2"}]}' \
  --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
```

The partition set is decided at instance creation by whoever supplies the
params, without the template changing.

## From the claim's own payload

```yaml
    claim_producers:
      - name: claim-producer-filesystem
        selector: queue
        intent: rw
        alias: job
    fan_out:
      claim: job
      partition_request: '{"list":[{"key":"{{claim.job.payload.folder}}-a"},
                                   {"key":"{{claim.job.payload.folder}}-b"}]}'
```

The producer puts the folder name in the claim payload; the author interpolates
it into the keys. Partitions can be named partly by what the claim producer
found.

## From a typed message body

```yaml
messages:
  - type: batch/requested
    body_schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        items: {type: array}
nodes:
  - type: fan_parent
    subscribes:
      - node: batch/requested
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    fan_out:
      claim: data
      partition_request: '{"list":{{messages.batch/requested.items}}}'
```

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"type":"batch/requested","payload":{"items":[{"key":"m-1"},{"key":"m-2"},{"key":"m-3"}]}}'
```

The caller sending the message decides the partition set at wake time.

## From a host-environment variable

```yaml
    fan_out:
      claim: data
      partition_request: '{"list":[{"key":"{{env.EXP_FANOUT_KEY}}-1"},
                                   {"key":"{{env.EXP_FANOUT_KEY}}-2"}]}'
```

Read from the deployment's own process environment, and resolves on the same
terms as the rest.

## The one source that cannot work here

`{{child.partition_key}}` is the fan-out's own output, so it cannot be an input
to the request that creates the partitions. Read it in the node's attributes, as
every example above does.
